title: Echo Sleuth Sidecar — Compact Error Triage Side Panel
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Design a lightweight, persistent side panel (the 'Echo Sleuth Sidecar') for the Redwood Console that accelerates error triage for failed requests and retry chains without requiring users to open the full diagnostics workspace. The panel should be readable at a glance, prioritize actionable signals, and surface compact payload diffs and error taxonomy clusters.

Problem statement: Current error debugging flows require users to navigate into heavyweight debug canvases to correlate retries, KV cache state, and payload deltas. Teams want a quick, low-distraction view in the main request list or trace detail that answers: are failures repeated, are retries changing input, which error class dominates, and is there an obvious mitigation (retry policy, fallback) available?

Core features proposed: 1) Retry Echoes strip — shows up to 5 recent attempts with micro-timelines and a colored health bar representing latency and outcome. 2) Error Echo Fingerprint — a compact badge that summarizes most common error class (e.g., Model OOM, Kernel Failure, BadRequest) with confidence score and a tooltip describing likely causes. 3) Payload SparkLens — a 1-row sparkline that highlights token-level anomaly spikes (for text generation) and a small diff teaser for request vs final attempt. 4) Quick Actions — contextual buttons (Re-run with same inputs, Re-run with cached prefix, Create rollback rule, Open full trace) with guardrails and suggested defaults. 5) Minimal artifact attachments — link to a lightweight payload snapshot (JSON minified), and a link to the full debug panel.

Design constraints and principles: - Compact: must fit in a 280px wide sidecar that docks to the right of request list/detail. - Non-blocking: initial load is low-bandwidth; only fetch full payload when user clicks the diff teaser. - Privacy by default: payload teasers mask sensitive fields; a disclosure explains masking. - Accessibility: all visuals must be keyboard and screen-reader accessible; color pairing uses WCAG AA contrast. - Extensibility: layout supports adding a small ML-derived root cause suggestion later.

Acceptance criteria: - Prototype in Figma with annotated component specs (spacing, tokens, states). - Usability test with 5 engineers showing >80% success on tasks: identify retry vs single-failure, surface likely error class, and start a re-run. - Design handoff tokens and redlines for engineering; components include micro-timeline, fingerprint token, sparklens, and action row.

Non-goals: Not intended to replace the full diagnostics canvas, not a replacement for long-term retention or heavy tracing visualizations.
comments: 2026-03-04 — Aisha Kumar: Initial concept draft uploaded to Figma. Focused on 3 signals (retries, error fingerprint, payload sparkline). Asked ENG/PM for performance constraints and a placeholder for privacy masking.

2026-03-05 — Liam O'Connor (Engineering): Reviewed prototype. Notes: micro-timeline must be renderable from existing trace aggregates; avoid per-token fetch for list render. Suggested server-side precompute for sparklens buckets. Assigned ENG-84120 to prototype backend endpoint.

2026-03-06 — Marta Reyes (Design): Iteration 2 uploaded — collapsed state for sidecar, condensed labels, keyboard focus order doc added. Updated color palette for error fingerprint to ensure AA contrast for red/amber/green states.

2026-03-08 — Priya Shah (PM): Concern about exposing sensitive prompt content in sparklens. Decision: teaser diffs will mask fields based on PII rules; add a per-organization toggle for full payload previews and an audit link. Added PM task PM-4021.

2026-03-09 — Accessibility review (external consultant): Requested explicit aria-labels for each action button, and announced state changes for dynamic sparklens updates. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-11 — Engineering review meeting notes (Liam): Backend precompute pipeline accepted; micro-timeline derives from span summary. Performance target: sidecar rendering under 120ms median in list view with caching. Edge-case: very long retry chains will truncate to most recent 5 attempts.

2026-03-12 — Aisha Kumar: Updated prototype with masked teaser UX, added CTA for 'Open full diagnostics' and a compact exploit mitigation suggestion card (e.g., 'enable KV cache warmup'). Ready for usability sessions; moving ticket to In Review.
2026-03-12 — QA lead (Noah Green): Added checklist to test plan — keyboard nav, masking toggles, failover when payload fetch 404s, and telemetry events for quick-actions clicks.
engineering_notes: Backend: ENG-84120 to produce /sidecar/summary API that returns compressed retry meta + sparklens histogram; payload fetch remains opt-in /sidecar/payload/{id}
Client: Render sidecar off a lightweight store slice; lazy-load full payload when user expands teaser. Implement optimistic UI for Quick Actions; show toast + link to long-running job.
Performance: aim for <120ms render for median; cap network calls per list page to N+1 where N is number of visible sidecars (lazy).
